Series::erfcinv¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::erfcinv() const
Series& Series::erfcinv_()

What It Does¶

Computes the inverse complementary error function elementwise. erfcinv is the functional inverse of erfc on the open interval (0, 2):

erfc( erfcinv(y) ) = y        for y in (0, 2)

It is erfinv shifted onto the complementary scale:

erfcinv(y) = erfinv(1 - y)

The reason to reach for erfcinv rather than erfinv(1 - y) is the far tail. When a routine works with a small upper-tail probability y directly — p-values, exceedance probabilities, the survival function of a Gaussian — forming 1 - y first loses precision, and for y below about 1e-16 collapses to exactly 1. erfcinv keeps the small argument intact and stays accurate where erfinv(1 - y) has already saturated.

Domain and endpoints:

  • erfcinv(1) = 0.

  • erfcinv is antisymmetric about y = 1: erfcinv(2 - y) = -erfcinv(y).

  • As y -> 0 the value goes to +inf; as y -> 2 it goes to -inf. erfcinv(0) returns +inf and erfcinv(2) returns -inf exactly.

  • Outside [0, 2] the inverse does not exist and erfcinv(y) returns NaN.

erfcinv() is out-of-place; erfcinv_() overwrites the current storage.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series or Series& A Series with the same shape as self. Interior arguments map to finite values, 0 and 2 to +/-inf, and y < 0 or y > 2 to NaN. erfcinv_() returns a reference to the mutated series.

An integral input is promoted to float64.

Gradient¶

erfcinv() is differentiable on the interior. It is the negative of the erfinv derivative evaluated at the same point, because d/dy (1 - y) = -1:

d/dy erfcinv(y) = -sqrt(pi)/2 * exp( erfcinv(y)^2 )

The slope is -sqrt(pi)/2 = -0.8862 at y = 1 and diverges toward either endpoint. At y = 0 or y = 2 the sensitivity is -inf; outside [0, 2] it is NaN.

Examples¶

Example 1. erfcinv(1) = 0; values below 1 are positive, above 1 negative.

pluss::series::print(std::cout,
                     pluss::make_series({1.0, 0.5, 1.5, 0.1}).erfcinv());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 0.4769, -0.4769, 1.1631]

Example 2. The identity erfcinv(y) = erfinv(1 - y), checked directly.

pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({0.3, 0.8, 1.4}).erfcinv());
pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({0.7, 0.2, -0.4}).erfinv());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.7329, 0.1791, -0.3708]
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.7329, 0.1791, -0.3708]

Example 3. Endpoints and out-of-domain arguments. 0 and 2 give +/-inf; anything outside [0, 2] gives NaN.

std::cout << pluss::make_series({0.0, 2.0, -0.5, 2.5}).erfcinv();

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[inf, -inf, nan, nan]

Example 4. The backward pass is -sqrt(pi)/2 * exp(erfcinv(y)^2). Because the factor depends on erfcinv(y)^2, arguments symmetric about 1 share a magnitude.

auto y = pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.0, 1.5});
y.tracks_slope_(true);
y.erfcinv().sum().reverse();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, y.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-1.1126, -0.8862, -1.1126]

Example 5. erfcinv_() overwrites the current storage in place.

auto a = pluss::make_series({1.0, 0.5, 2.0});
a.erfcinv_();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, a);

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0000, 0.4769, -inf]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The domain is [0, 2], not [-1, 1]. It is a complementary-scale inverse: the argument is a tail mass, not a signed value.

  • y < 0 or y > 2 returns NaN; 0 and 2 return +/-inf.

  • The whole reason to use erfcinv over erfinv(1 - y) is precision for tiny y. If you have already formed 1 - y, that precision is gone — pass the small quantity straight in.

  • The gradient diverges toward both endpoints.

  • Integral inputs promote to float64.

Summary¶

erfcinv() inverts erfc on (0, 2):

  • erfcinv(y) = erfinv(1 - y), but accurate for small y

  • erfcinv(1) = 0, erfcinv(0) = +inf, erfcinv(2) = -inf

  • y outside [0, 2] returns NaN

  • differentiable on the interior with backward -sqrt(pi)/2 * exp(erfcinv(y)^2)

  • erfcinv_() is the in-place form
